title: Authentication request reveals parent role to the authentication endpoint
description: The /api/auth request can expose that the data subject is acting in the parent role through identifiers, request parameters, headers, or contextual metadata. This allows the receiving process to identify or single out the user and associate the account with a sensitive role.
assumptions: Assumes the authentication request includes or implies the actor role, account identifier, email/phone, device token, or similar identifying data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a best-fit for identification via direct identifiers in an authentication flow; exact node may vary depending on the concrete data items sent.

title: Login request discloses sensitive personal data to the authentication process
description: Authentication traffic commonly contains personal data such as username, email address, phone number, role information, and possibly credentials or authentication secrets. Processing this request may disclose personal data beyond what is strictly necessary if the API design is verbose or over-collects attributes.
assumptions: Assumes /api/auth accepts identifiers and possibly role/context attributes from the parent actor.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for unnecessary or broad personal-data exposure in a message flow; exact node depends on the implementation details of the auth request payload.

title: Authentication request enables linkability across sessions or services
description: Persistent identifiers in the auth request, such as account IDs, email addresses, device identifiers, or stable cookies, can let the authentication process link multiple login attempts and potentially correlate the parent across sessions, devices, or related services.
assumptions: Assumes stable identifiers or tokens are transmitted with the request.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability based on repeated stable identifiers in a flow; exact sub-node may differ if the linkability arises from metadata rather than explicit identifiers.

title: Authentication endpoint may become aware of the parent's activity or intent
description: By requesting /api/auth, the parent reveals that they are attempting to access the system at a specific time. Timing, frequency, source metadata, and role context may allow the process to detect behavioral patterns such as active usage windows, retries, or household routines.
assumptions: Assumes request metadata and timestamps are logged or observable by the process.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability node for observability of a subject's action from network/application metadata; exact node may differ in a full threat tree.

title: Parent may be unaware of identity, metadata, or role information sent during authentication
description: The parent may not understand what personal data the /api/auth call transmits or infers, such as device details, IP-derived location, identifiers, or role attributes. This creates a risk that processing is not sufficiently transparent to the user.
assumptions: Assumes the system does not clearly explain the data collected and inferred during login.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node for insufficient transparency during collection in an auth flow; exact node may vary by the tree version used.

title: Authentication request may collect more data than necessary for the stated purpose
description: If /api/auth requests excessive personal data, long-lived identifiers, or role/context attributes beyond what is required to authenticate the parent, the flow may violate data minimization or purpose-limitation expectations.
assumptions: Assumes the endpoint design or logging retains unnecessary attributes associated with the auth request.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node for data minimization/purpose limitation concerns in an authentication collection flow; exact sub-node depends on the compliance focus.

title: Lack of adequate evidence about what was presented during authentication can create repudiation issues
description: If the system does not record what notices, consent prompts, or authentication assertions were shown and submitted, the parent or the service may later be unable to prove what personal-data processing or account action was agreed to at login.
assumptions: Assumes the authentication interaction has legal or policy significance and records are incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central for a simple auth request than other categories; included as a possible privacy-relevant threat only if the flow carries assertions, notices, or agreements.

title: Authentication response may disclose personal data to an unintended recipient
description: The /api/auth response to the parent actor may include personal data or account attributes (for example user identifier, email, profile details, roles, or session state). If the response is sent to the wrong parent context, intercepted at the client side, or exposed through overly broad response contents, personal information is disclosed.
assumptions: Assumes the authentication response can contain identifying/account-related data beyond a simple success indicator.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for data disclosure in a return flow, but exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may vary.

title: Authentication response enables identification of the user
description: If /api/auth returns stable identifiers, usernames, email addresses, account IDs, or similarly unique attributes to the parent actor, the data flow directly identifies the user or makes them readily identifiable.
assumptions: Assumes the response contains direct or indirect identifiers rather than an anonymous boolean-only result.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best match for identification through disclosed identifiers.

title: Authentication response can be linked to other interactions or accounts
description: Returned account identifiers, persistent session identifiers, or stable tokens may let the parent link this authentication event with prior or future actions, profiles, or data from other contexts.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers or tokens are persistent enough to support correlation across sessions or services.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for linkability via stable identifiers/tokens; exact subnode may differ.

title: Authentication error details may disclose account existence or sensitive state
description: If /api/auth returns different messages or metadata for invalid password, unknown account, locked account, MFA required, or disabled user, the parent can learn sensitive facts about a person's account status or existence.
assumptions: Assumes the endpoint exposes distinguishable error responses or state-specific details.
uncertainty_note: Chosen as a disclosure-by-response-content node; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Parent may be unaware of what authentication data is returned and for what purpose
description: The flow may return more authentication-related or profile data than the parent actor expects or understands, reducing predictability and user awareness about which personal data is being shared after authentication.
assumptions: Assumes there is limited transparency to the user/parent about response fields and their purpose.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness applies if the response contents are not clearly communicated; node id is approximate.

title: Authentication response may violate data minimization or purpose limitation
description: If /api/auth returns excessive personal data to the parent role when only an authentication result or minimal claims are necessary, the flow may be non-compliant with privacy requirements such as data minimization, necessity, or purpose limitation.
assumptions: Assumes only a subset of returned attributes is necessary for the parent to perform its function.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort non-compliance node selection based on excessive response data.

title: Subprofile request can reveal the child has multiple profile contexts
description: A request to /api/subprofiles may disclose that the child account has subprofiles or segmented profile data. If observed by network intermediaries, logs, analytics systems, or internal operators, the mere fact that this endpoint is invoked can reveal personal circumstances or account structure about the child.
assumptions: Assumes the endpoint path or associated metadata is visible in request logs, telemetry, or to parties beyond the strictly necessary recipient.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is my best fit for disclosure of sensitive personal information via communication metadata; exact LINDDUN Pro node label may vary.

title: Repeated subprofile requests may enable linkability of the child across sessions
description: If the request carries stable identifiers such as account IDs, device IDs, session tokens, or consistent network metadata, repeated calls to /api/subprofiles can be linked to the same child over time, enabling correlation of activity patterns.
assumptions: Assumes stable identifiers or quasi-identifiers are present in headers, tokens, IP metadata, or application logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for linkability/identifiability through persistent identifiers in a data flow.

title: Subprofile request may be linkable with other API activity
description: The child’s request to /api/subprofiles can be correlated with other requests from the same device, account, or network context, linking this action with broader behavior such as play history, parental controls use, or account management events.
assumptions: Assumes backend, CDN, or observability systems retain shared identifiers across flows.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to capture cross-context linkability of this flow with other events.

title: The child may be unaware that requesting subprofiles exposes profile-structure metadata
description: The user may not understand that invoking /api/subprofiles can expose metadata about available subprofiles, account organization, or usage context to the service and its supporting infrastructure, reducing transparency and predictability of processing.
assumptions: Assumes the interface does not clearly explain what data is sent or inferred when loading subprofiles.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to an unawareness/transparency threat node.

title: Collection of subprofile-request data may exceed what is necessary for the child's request
description: If /api/subprofiles logs or collects excessive request metadata beyond what is required to return the child’s subprofiles, the processing may violate data minimization or purpose-limitation expectations, especially given the child context.
assumptions: Assumes request handling includes extensive logging, analytics, or reuse of request data for secondary purposes.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to represent non-compliance through over-collection or secondary use on this flow.

title: Unnecessary disclosure of subprofile data to the child role
description: The /api/subprofiles endpoint returns data about subprofiles to the child role. If the response includes more attributes than needed, sensitive details about other profiles or household members may be exposed to the child.
assumptions: Assumes subprofiles may contain personal data beyond the minimum needed by the child user.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is a best-effort estimate for disclosure via data flow/response content; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Child may be unaware of what personal data is contained in returned subprofiles
description: The API response may provide subprofile data without sufficient transparency about which fields are included, where the data originated, or how it will be used, limiting the child's awareness of processing.
assumptions: Assumes the consuming interface does not clearly explain the contents and purpose of returned subprofile data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to unawareness; exact node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Return of subprofile data may be incompatible with consent or authorization boundaries
description: If /api/subprofiles returns data for profiles that the child is not permitted to access, or returns fields beyond those covered by consent/parental authorization, the processing may violate policy or legal basis constraints.
assumptions: Assumes access control, parental consent, or purpose limitation requirements apply to child access to subprofile data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to non-compliance; exact node id may differ.

title: Subprofile response may enable identification of another person
description: Data returned to the child may directly or indirectly identify another individual represented by a subprofile, especially if names, dates, relationship details, or unique attributes are included.
assumptions: Assumes subprofiles can represent other data subjects and include identifying or quasi-identifying attributes.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to identifiability; exact node id may differ.

title: Returned subprofile attributes may allow linkage across contexts
description: A child receiving stable identifiers or distinctive attributes in subprofile data may be able to correlate the subprofile with records from other contexts, linking information about the same person across systems or views.
assumptions: Assumes the response contains stable IDs or sufficiently distinctive combinations of attributes.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to linkability; exact node id may differ.

title: Presence or absence of subprofiles may reveal detectability of hidden relationships or account state
description: Even if detailed data is minimized, the mere fact that /api/subprofiles returns one or more entries can reveal that certain profiles exist, that the child is associated with them, or that a household/account relationship is present.
assumptions: Assumes existence of subprofiles or their count is itself sensitive.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to detectability; exact node id may differ.

title: Subprofile request reveals existence of child-related data to an unauthorized requester
description: If /api/subprofiles responds differently depending on whether the parent has associated child subprofiles, the request/response interaction may disclose the existence or absence of personal data about a child or household relationship to someone using the parent role without proper authorization checks.
assumptions: Assumes the endpoint behavior, status codes, timing, or payload differ based on whether subprofiles exist or whether the requester is entitled to view them.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for data disclosure via unauthorized access to returned personal data; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree labeling may vary.

title: Subprofile request can reveal whether multiple requests come from the same parent
description: Identifiers such as session tokens, stable account IDs, device identifiers, or consistent request metadata sent with calls to /api/subprofiles may allow the process to link repeated requests to the same parent account and build a profile of access patterns.
assumptions: Assumes authentication or transport/application metadata contains stable identifiers and that linkage beyond what is necessary is a privacy concern in scope.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort choice for identifiability/linkability from persistent identifiers in a request flow.

title: Request metadata may enable linking the parent to child subprofiles
description: The fact that a specific authenticated parent requests /api/subprofiles can link that parent identity to one or more child-related subprofiles or family relationships, especially if logs or analytics retain the association.
assumptions: Assumes the endpoint is specifically for retrieving child or dependent subprofiles and that logs/analytics persist requester identity with endpoint usage.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for linkability between two data subjects/entities via endpoint use; exact tree node may differ.

title: Request endpoint and parameters may allow detecting a parent's family status
description: Observing that a user accesses /api/subprofiles, or observing distinct responses from that endpoint, may allow an observer or internal analyst to deduce that the requester is a parent/guardian and infer family composition or presence of dependents.
assumptions: Assumes endpoint names, routing, logs, or traffic metadata are visible to operators, analysts, or other observers, and that access to this endpoint is correlated with having dependents.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability of sensitive status from endpoint usage; exact subtree may vary.

title: Parent may not be adequately informed that subprofile access is logged or used beyond service delivery
description: When requesting /api/subprofiles, the parent may be unaware that the request, associated identifiers, and inferred family relationships are logged, analyzed, or shared for secondary purposes, resulting in insufficient transparency or consent alignment.
assumptions: Assumes notice/consent mechanisms are incomplete or do not specifically cover logging, analytics, or secondary use of this access event.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort non-compliance classification based on potential lack of transparency/consent; exact node id may differ.

title: Parent could deny having requested subprofiles if request logging is inadequate
description: If the system does not maintain trustworthy audit records for calls to /api/subprofiles, the parent may later deny making the request, undermining accountability for access to child-related profile data.
assumptions: Assumes accountability for access to subprofile data is required and current logging or evidence quality may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less commonly emphasized as a pure privacy harm for a simple request flow, so applicability is moderate and node id is best-effort.

title: Parent may be unaware of the privacy implications of requesting subprofiles
description: The interface or API interaction may not make clear what categories of child-related personal data will be retrieved, why they are needed, or what inferences can be drawn from the request itself, leaving the parent insufficiently aware.
assumptions: Assumes the request is initiated through a client experience that may lack contextual privacy information or just-in-time explanation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort classification under unawareness; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Disclosure of child subprofile data to the wrong parent
description: The /api/subprofiles response may expose a child's subprofile data to a parent who is not authorized for that specific child or account relationship, if authorization checks are weak, missing, or based on manipulable identifiers.
assumptions: The endpoint returns personal data about one or more child subprofiles and parent access depends on a verified relationship or authorization context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure via unauthorized access; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree wording may differ.

title: Excessive disclosure in subprofile response
description: The response to the parent may include more attributes than necessary, such as internal identifiers, sensitive child metadata, behavioral information, timestamps, or hidden profile fields, increasing privacy exposure beyond the intended purpose.
assumptions: The API may serialize full subprofile objects unless fields are minimized per role and purpose.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for over-disclosure/data minimization failure rather than a precisely verified catalog entry.

title: Subprofile records can be linked to a specific family or child across contexts
description: Data returned to the parent may contain stable identifiers or distinctive attribute combinations that allow the parent, or anyone later gaining access to the response, to link the subprofile to other records, sessions, or external datasets concerning the same child or household.
assumptions: Returned data includes persistent IDs or sufficiently unique attributes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit linkability node id; exact subtree number may vary in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Interception of subprofile data in transit or at the client side
description: If transport security, caching controls, or client-side storage handling are insufficient, the subprofile data returned to the parent could be exposed to network attackers, shared devices, browser extensions, or other unintended recipients.
assumptions: Threat includes practical exposure through insecure transport configuration, proxy caching, or unsafe client storage/display on the parent's side.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is an approximate best fit for disclosure during transfer or endpoint exposure.

title: Subprofile response enables identification of a child
description: Even if the service intends only to show account subprofiles, the returned data may directly identify the child through name, photo, exact age, contact details, or other direct identifiers.
assumptions: Subprofiles belong to natural persons and contain direct identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit identifiability node id; exact numbering may differ.

title: Combination of returned attributes makes the child identifiable
description: Attributes in the subprofile response that are not direct identifiers on their own, such as age band, school, language, avatar, preferences, and activity timestamps, may in combination single out and identify the child.
assumptions: The parent or another party can combine quasi-identifiers with external knowledge.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node selection for indirect identifiability via quasi-identifiers.

title: Return of subprofile data without consent or legal-basis alignment
description: The endpoint may return child subprofile information to the parent without verifying that the sharing is covered by the applicable consent state, custody arrangement, age-related rules, or other legal basis and policy constraints.
assumptions: Access to child data may be conditioned by consent, parental rights, or jurisdiction-specific rules.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node id; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may differ.

title: Parent is not adequately informed about the scope of returned child data
description: The API response may omit or obscure which categories of child data are being returned and why, making it hard for the parent to understand the extent of processing and downstream use.
assumptions: Transparency duties apply and API/UI layers may not clearly explain fields or purposes.
uncertainty_note: Approximate best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency associated with this flow.

title: Excessive identity disclosure in user-list response
description: A request to /api/users by a parent role may cause the API to reveal direct identifiers of multiple users (for example names, usernames, emails, internal IDs) beyond what is necessary for the parent's purpose. This discloses personal data to the requester and increases privacy risk for all listed users.
assumptions: Assumes the endpoint returns user records containing direct identifiers and that the parent role is not strictly limited to only those users it is authorized to view.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identity disclosure via data content; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ depending on whether the implementation returns direct or indirect identifiers.

title: Attribute disclosure through overbroad user data returned by /api/users
description: The endpoint may return privacy-sensitive attributes about users, such as child/parent relationship, age band, class membership, contact details, account status, or other profile fields, when responding to a parent request. Even if direct identifiers are minimized, these attributes themselves may disclose personal information.
assumptions: Assumes the API response includes profile or relationship attributes beyond the minimum needed for the requesting parent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for attribute disclosure; exact subnode depends on the actual schema returned by /api/users.

title: Linkability of multiple users via common response context
description: Returning a list of users to one parent can allow the requester to link several individuals together within one shared context, such as inferring which children belong to the same household, class, or service cohort. Stable internal identifiers in the response can further enable correlation across sessions or datasets.
assumptions: Assumes /api/users returns multiple records and includes stable identifiers or shared contextual fields that permit correlation.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; linkability may also map to a more specific subnode if stable identifiers or metadata are present.

title: User enumeration through /api/users access
description: A parent calling /api/users may be able to learn whether specific individuals exist in the system, or infer the size and composition of the user population, even without full profile access. This can make users identifiable or confirm their participation in the service.
assumptions: Assumes the endpoint returns a user list or distinguishable results that reveal account existence or membership.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability via existence/listing. Exact subnode may differ based on whether identification is direct or inferential.

title: Unawareness of user-list sharing with parent role
description: Users whose records are returned by /api/users may be unaware that their data can be disclosed to a parent role, what categories of data are shared, and for what purpose. Lack of clear notice reduces their understanding and ability to exercise privacy choices.
assumptions: Assumes users are not clearly informed that a parent-role requester can access their data through this endpoint.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate because unawareness in LINDDUN Pro can be split across notice, visibility, or expectation-related subnodes.

title: Processing user data beyond consent or authorization scope
description: If /api/users returns records for users outside the parent's legitimate relationship or beyond the purposes originally communicated and authorized, the processing may violate consent, permissions, or purpose-limitation expectations. This creates a non-compliance risk in addition to the disclosure itself.
assumptions: Assumes there are policy, consent, or legal constraints limiting which user data a parent may access and for what purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance/purpose overreach; exact subnode depends on the governing policy and legal basis.

title: Disclosure of user data to the parent role beyond necessity
description: The /api/users endpoint returns user-related data to a parent actor. If the response includes more attributes than needed for the parent's purpose, personal data may be disclosed unnecessarily to the recipient.
assumptions: Assumes the response may contain personal data about one or more users and that data minimization is not strictly enforced.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for excessive attribute disclosure may differ.

title: Unawareness of affected users about sharing with parent
description: If users are not clearly informed that their data can be returned by /api/users to a parent-role recipient, they may be unaware of this disclosure and its scope.
assumptions: Assumes the data subjects are users whose data is returned and privacy notices or in-context transparency may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort transparency/unawareness mapping from memory.

title: Non-compliant transfer of user data to parent
description: Returning user data to a parent may violate purpose limitation, consent, lawful basis, or least-privilege requirements if the parent is not authorized to receive all returned fields or records.
assumptions: Assumes jurisdictional or policy requirements apply to user data disclosures and authorization may be broader in implementation than permitted by policy.
uncertainty_note: Exact compliance subtree id may differ; classification is confident but node id is approximate.

title: Identifiability of users in API response
description: The response may contain direct or indirect identifiers that allow the parent to identify individual users, even if only aggregate or limited information was needed.
assumptions: Assumes response fields may include names, emails, IDs, or combinations of quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit identifiability node id from memory; exact node may be more specific.

title: Linkability of user records across requests or systems
description: Stable identifiers in the /api/users response may enable the parent to correlate records across sessions, endpoints, or external datasets, linking activity or profiles belonging to the same user.
assumptions: Assumes stable identifiers or consistent attribute combinations are present in responses.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit linkability node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Admin identity exposed to the user-management service through authenticated request metadata
description: When the admin requests /api/users, the receiving process can identify which specific administrator initiated the action via session tokens, client certificates, usernames, IP addresses, or other request metadata. If this identification is unnecessary or overly granular for the purpose, the flow creates an identifiability risk for the admin.
assumptions: Assumes the request carries authentication or contextual metadata that can directly or indirectly identify the individual admin.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best estimate for identifiability of a data flow; exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node may differ.

title: Repeated /api/users requests can be linked to the same administrator
description: If the process observes stable identifiers such as account IDs, session identifiers, device fingerprints, or source network attributes, it can link multiple /api/users requests to the same admin over time. This enables behavioral profiling of administrative activity.
assumptions: Assumes stable identifiers or correlatable metadata are present across requests.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for linkability; exact sub-node may vary in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Administrative query reveals role or privileges of the requester
description: A request to /api/users is likely restricted to privileged staff. Observing this flow may allow the process or supporting infrastructure to infer that the requester has an administrative role, which discloses an attribute about the individual beyond the immediate purpose of the request.
assumptions: Assumes access to /api/users is limited to admins or elevated roles and that this fact is privacy-relevant.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for detectability/disclosure-by-observation; exact node may differ.

title: Use of admin request metadata beyond user-list retrieval may lack transparency or valid basis
description: The request may include personal data about the admin, such as identifiers, IP address, device information, and audit context. If these data are collected, retained, or repurposed for monitoring, analytics, or secondary uses without proper notice, minimization, or legal basis, the flow can create non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes the system processes personal data in the request context and applicable privacy obligations require purpose limitation, transparency, and minimization.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate because non-compliance nodes are framework-specific in some LINDDUN Pro variants.

title: Admin may be unable to plausibly deny the request due to strong auditability
description: If the request is strongly bound to the administrator through detailed logs, signatures, or tamper-resistant audit trails, the admin cannot later deny having performed the action. While often desirable for security and accountability, this can also be a privacy threat under non-repudiation because the action becomes permanently attributable.
assumptions: Assumes comprehensive logging or cryptographic proof is attached to the request.
uncertainty_note: Included from a LINDDUN perspective even though non-repudiation is often intentionally added for security; exact node id may differ.

title: Excessive disclosure of user data in /api/users response
description: The /api/users endpoint may return more personal data about users than the admin needs for the intended task, exposing unnecessary attributes or full records to the admin.
assumptions: Assumes the response can include personal data fields beyond the minimum necessary for administrative use.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-effort; I am using a generic disclosure node because the exact LINDDUN Pro subtree variant depends on the catalog version.

title: Admin cannot determine why specific user data is shown
description: If the API response lacks contextual information about purpose, legal basis, or source of the returned user data, the admin may be unable to understand why particular personal data is included, reducing intervenability and informed handling.
assumptions: Assumes the system does not provide metadata or explanation alongside returned user data.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; unawareness subtrees vary between LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Returned user data may exceed consent, role, or policy constraints
description: The endpoint may disclose user records to the admin in a way that is inconsistent with privacy policy, consent, purpose limitation, or role-based access rules, creating non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes some users' data may be subject to restrictions not enforced by the endpoint response logic.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection; exact non-compliance subtree id may differ by taxonomy edition.

title: Admin can link records across users or datasets
description: By receiving stable identifiers or rich attribute combinations in the /api/users response, the admin can link records about the same individuals across sessions, internal datasets, or exported data, increasing privacy risk beyond the immediate task.
assumptions: Assumes the response contains persistent identifiers or quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Generic linkability node used; exact child node may differ depending on whether the emphasis is identifiers, metadata, or correlation.

title: User records may be identifiable in the response
description: The response may contain direct identifiers such as names, email addresses, account IDs, or combinations of attributes that make individual users identifiable to the admin or anyone who gains access to the admin context.
assumptions: Assumes /api/users returns personal data tied to individual accounts.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort generic identifiability node; exact LINDDUN Pro child node depends on whether direct or indirect identifiers are modeled.

title: Returned dataset may enable inference of sensitive user attributes
description: Even if the response omits explicit sensitive fields, combinations of returned attributes, statuses, roles, activity markers, or group memberships may allow the admin to detect or infer sensitive information about users.
assumptions: Assumes the endpoint returns sufficiently rich data for inference.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; detectability/discoverability branches are version-dependent.

description: If the system does not log which user records and attributes were returned by /api/users to the admin, the admin or system operator may later be able to deny having disclosed specific personal data, hindering auditability and accountability.
assumptions: Assumes response disclosures are not fully logged with sufficient detail and integrity protection.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection; repudiation subtree naming can vary across sources.

description: A request from a parent to the /api/videos endpoint may reveal that this user is seeking video resources, and depending on request parameters, may disclose interests, child-related context, or other sensitive preferences to the receiving process and anyone able to observe request contents.
assumptions: Assumes the request may include query parameters, filters, authentication context, or metadata that can expose preferences or family-related context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id. Exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether the endpoint supports detailed search/filter parameters.

description: If requests to /api/videos contain stable identifiers, session tokens, IP address patterns, device fingerprints, or consistent behavioral characteristics, the process can link multiple requests to the same parent over time and build a viewing-interest profile.
assumptions: Assumes the system logs or observes persistent identifiers or metadata across requests.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability via message metadata/identifiers.

title: Request metadata may allow detection of the parent's activity
description: Observation of traffic to /api/videos may let the process itself, operators, or network observers detect that a parent is currently active and using the video feature, even if the exact content returned is not known.
assumptions: Assumes request timing, endpoint path, or network metadata are observable by relevant parties.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability of communication existence/activity.

title: Parent may be unaware of logging or profiling of video requests
description: The parent may not understand that requests to /api/videos are logged, analyzed for recommendations, or correlated with account and device data, reducing transparency about how personal data is processed.
assumptions: Assumes notice is incomplete, unclear, or not presented in context of the request.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact subtree depends on the project's LINDDUN Pro catalog for insufficient information/transparency.

title: Video request processing may exceed stated purpose or lack valid basis
description: If the /api/videos request data is retained, reused for analytics/marketing, or combined with other family-account data beyond what is necessary to serve the request, the processing may violate data minimization, purpose limitation, or lawful-basis requirements.
assumptions: Assumes governance controls may be insufficient and that request data is personal data under applicable regulation.
